summary:
TerraShift is a climate-informed crop rotation decision-support platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It uses NASA POWER daily climate data for Story County, Iowa, covering 1991–2025, to help users explore historical climate patterns and agricultural rotation systems.

Our Python data pipeline processes 12,784 daily climate records, applies quality checks and calculates seasonal indicators such as precipitation, growing degree days and dry spells. A Next.js web application presents climate insights, a growing-season calendar, three crop rotation systems and printable reports.

TerraShift makes historical climate information more accessible and supports better-informed agricultural planning. It clearly distinguishes available climate data from pending rotation evidence. The current MVP is county-level decision support, not a validated farm-specific recommendation or crop-yield prediction system.
details:
TerraShift — Project Details

Problem and Motivation

Agricultural planning is affected by changing climate conditions. Historical temperature, rainfall, humidity and seasonal patterns can help people understand the environment in which crop rotations are explored. However, climate information and crop rotation information are often difficult to interpret together.

TerraShift addresses this challenge by building a climate-informed crop rotation decision-support platform for Story County, Iowa.

How It Works

TerraShift uses NASA POWER daily climate data for the county's internal point (42.0375, -93.4661), covering 1991–2025.

A Python processing pipeline fetches the original climate response, validates and cleans daily measurements, applies quality-control rules and produces a structured CSV dataset. The pipeline also generates seasonal environmental summaries and crop rotation comparison data.

The application processes 12,784 daily climate records across 35 growing seasons. Its climate indicators include temperature, precipitation, relative humidity, wind speed, solar radiation, growing degree days and dry spells.

A Next.js web application presents the processed information through:

  • Pilot Region information.
  • NASA Climate Insights and historical climate charts.
  • Three crop rotation systems.
  • Growing-season crop calendar.
  • Printable pilot reports.

Crop Rotation Systems

The platform displays three systems:

  1. Two-year Corn–Soybean baseline.
  2. Three-year Corn–Soybean–Oat with Red Clover.
  3. Four-year Corn–Soybean–Oat with Alfalfa.

Rotation-specific comparison evidence is currently pending approval. TerraShift deliberately avoids unsupported yield predictions or claims that one rotation is superior.

Technology Used

Python, NASA POWER API, Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, pytest and Vitest.

Innovation and Intended Impact

TerraShift combines historical NASA climate information, transparent data processing, seasonal visualization and crop rotation exploration in one accessible interface.

Its intended impact is to make climate information easier to understand and provide a foundation for better-informed agricultural planning. Future development will focus on validated soil information, land-cover integration, crop-history datasets and field-level validation with agricultural experts.

Limitations

Climate information represents a NASA POWER grid cell at the county internal point, not individual farms. Soil wetness is a model estimate rather than a direct measurement. The current MVP is exploratory decision support and is not a validated farm-specific recommendation or crop-yield forecasting system.
